category_title: Medicated student struggling with ADHD diagnosis and agency
minimal_context: Dennis is participating in a Danish lesson where the class is using a camera with a cardboard cover.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Dennis, you took the cardboard cover off the camera. The instruction was to leave it on.

STUDENT: I do bad things. I am noisy.

TUTOR: Since you didn't follow the instructions, you need to go sit in the chair in the corner by the blackboard.

STUDENT: In school they keep an eye on me all the time, so that I do not do stupid things. All the time, I am afraid of doing stupid things and being yelled at.

TUTOR: Please just sit in the corner and face away from the class.

STUDENT: (Accepts being put in the corner in a chair at the blackboard, head faced away from class) I didn't mind. Then I do not have to be afraid of doing stupid things.

options.A: Use a healing-lake visualization during the Danish lesson, encouraging the student to observe that it is always changing yet always itself.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each task during the Danish lesson and related camera activities.
options.C: Use collective biography and student-taken photos to explore social self-understanding and reasons for action in a group setting.
options.D: Implement cooperative learning as an alternative strategy to structure the Danish lesson and related camera activities.
